config_name: Aspire Go 15.6" — Ryzen 5 40, 16GB LPDDR5, 1TB SSD, FHD IPS

specs.ports: 2x USB-C 3.2 Gen2 (DP, 45W PD), 1x USB-A 3.2 Gen1, 1x USB 2.0, HDMI 1.4, 3.5mm
specs.keyboard_notes: Chiclet with numeric keypad, bilingual CA

battery.notes: ~45 Wh. The 4-core Zen 2 chip sips power: ~6.5-7.5h light web/video despite modest pack.

price.notes: No sale; $999.99 flat. Priced above the Ryzen 7 7730U Mid twin ($799.95 on BF sale): newer Mendocino-refresh SKU at flat MSRP while the older SKU is discounted — spec hierarchy (tier Entry) kept per CPU capability.

offers.name: Acer Aspire Go 15.6" Laptop - Silver (AMD R5 40/16GB RAM/1TB SSD/Windows 11)

reviews.quote: Office notebook with long runtimes — very good battery runtimes and USB-C Power Delivery in a cheap 15.6-inch package.
This $300 laptop is a killer value and doesn't feel like a cheap laptop.
Nothing exciting, but it has clear value — a worthy machine for $300.

praises: 16GB + 1TB at $999.99 is the storage/RAM bargain of the Aspire line
Battery runs long (~7h) because the 4-core Mendocino chip barely draws power at idle
Cool and near-silent for browsing, docs, and streaming
Both USB-C ports do DisplayPort video and PD charging
IPS FHD panel still beats the TN panels on rival entry 15.6" machines
complaints: Ryzen 5 40 is only 4 cores / 4 threads — heavy tabs-plus-video calls stutter noticeably
LPDDR5 is soldered: 16GB is the permanent ceiling despite the roomy 1TB drive
Only one full-size USB-A port; the second is USB 2.0 speed
Heaviest chassis of the family at 1.73 kg despite the low-power internals
Dull 45%-gamut IPS panel and 720p webcam match nothing above the entry tier

standouts: Best RAM+storage per dollar in the Aspire family (16GB/1TB under $1,000) with genuinely long battery for the class
design_philosophy: Acer's low-power high-capacity entry: a 4-core Zen 2 Mendocino part that trades CPU muscle for battery life and silence, wrapped in the standard Go 15 chassis with an unusually generous 16GB/1TB spec. It suits light users who keep many files but do little computation.
rating_notes: No pro review found (see SHARED-aspire-go.md). Inferred from 7730U Go 15 sibling: −1.8 productivity (4C/4T Zen 2 vs 8C/16T Zen 3), +1.5 battery and +2.5 thermals for the ultra-low-draw Mendocino part on ~45Wh, −0.8 gaming (610M vs Vega 8), −2.0 upgradability (soldered LPDDR5 vs SO-DIMM). Battery hours class-estimated.
